title: Evaluation of the normalized sum polynomial
statement: Let $n\ge0$, let $\Omega$ be a measurable space, and let $X_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be arbitrary functions for $i=0,\ldots,n-1$. For every $\omega\in\Omega$, the multilinear polynomial whose singleton coefficients are $1/\sqrt n$ and whose other coefficients are zero evaluates to $\bigl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}X_i(\omega)\bigr)/\sqrt n$, with the usual real division convention when $n=0$.
hypotheses_covered: $X$ is any family of real-valued functions indexed by the $n$ coordinates
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\Omega$ be a measurable space, and let $X_i:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be arbitrary functions. The multilinear polynomial with singleton coefficients $1/\sqrt n$ and all other coefficients zero evaluates at $(X_i(\omega))_i$ to $\sum_iX_i(\omega)/\sqrt n$ for every $\omega\in\Omega$, with division by zero equal to zero.
